verdict.rationale: RudderStack ships its own event-level automation. Tracking Plans let you define rules that automatically flag, and act on, non-compliant incoming events, and Transformations run custom JavaScript or Python on every event in flight to filter, enrich or reshape it before delivery. However, the evidence shows no general-purpose rule builder where a user sets event conditions that trigger arbitrary downstream actions; the actions documented are limited to data-quality enforcement and code-based event shaping. Missing for 10: a documented declarative trigger/condition→action rules engine, a range of actions beyond filter/transform/flag, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Define your ideal state with shared data definitions and automatically flag violations on incoming data.
Tracking Plans Monitor and act on non-compliant event data at the source
Set predefined tracking plans to catch issues in transit, then fix and filter data before it impact downstream teams.
Transformations let you filter, enrich, and reshape event data before it reaches your destinations.
